description:
AI could make companies dramatically more productive. But what happens when the workers being replaced are also the customers keeping the economy alive?

Across corporate America, companies are cutting white-collar jobs while investing heavily in automation. AI systems can produce more without mortgages, car payments, or credit cards, and unlike human workers, they don’t spend their salaries back into the economy. That creates a dangerous imbalance. Former Google X executive Mo Gawdat has warned that widespread AI adoption could eliminate huge numbers of entry-level and professional jobs before new economic systems are ready to replace them. At the same time, AI could push more income toward company owners while workers receive a smaller share.

The economy may keep growing, but if fewer people can afford to participate in it, capitalism itself starts to look very different.

author: The Infographics Show
description:
MIT looked at what AI is actually replacing, and the answer isn’t entire professions. It’s entry-level work.

Researchers mapped more than 32,000 skills across 923 occupations and found that AI is especially capable of handling the structured tasks traditionally given to junior employees. Drafting documents, compiling data, basic coding, and administrative work. Senior workers are often benefiting instead. AI makes experienced lawyers, engineers, analysts, and managers faster and more productive, reducing the need to hire people underneath them. That creates a dangerous problem. Entry-level jobs were never just cheap labor, they were how graduates gained experience and became tomorrow’s managers and executives.

AI may not be destroying the corporate ladder, it may be removing the bottom rung.
